get.description:
The protected walking-skeleton read. Not audited: a GET of your own
identity is not a state change, and auditing every read would bury the
mutations the log exists for (ADR-BOS-009 audits *mutations*).

Archived companies are hidden by default (`status=active`); pass
`status=archived` or `status=all` to see them.

post.description:
The only route that creates a company. See
`service.provision_company`'s docstring for the atomicity guarantee this
wraps unchanged.

put.description:
Grant one module entitlement. Idempotent: calling this again on an
already-active module is a harmless no-op (`changed=False` in the
response), not an error.

delete.description:
Revoke one module entitlement. Idempotent, symmetric to
`grant_entitlement`. Never touches subscription state (ADR-BOS-010
§Decision 3) — a company can lose one module while remaining fully paid
up on everything else.

post.description:
Transition a company's subscription lifecycle state (trial / active /
grace_period / suspended / cancelled) — always with a mandatory reason.
One endpoint, not one per state ("suspend", "reactivate", ...): the
operation is the same reasoned-change shape regardless of direction, and
the console's suspend/reactivate buttons are just this call with a
different `new_state`.

put.description:
Set a company's seat limit. `null` means unlimited. Idempotent in
effect but always audited, even when the new value equals the current
one (mirrors `grant_entitlement`/`revoke_entitlement`, not the
reasoned-transition shape of subscription lifecycle changes — there is
no mandatory reason here).

Archive a company — a logical/soft archive, never a delete. No user,
session, subscription, entitlement or business-data row is touched.
Idempotent in effect but always audited, even when the company was
already archived.

Restore an archived company. Idempotent, symmetric to
`archive_company`.

schema.title: Response Logout Api V1 Auth Logout Post

post.description:
Tenant self-service: set or replace the caller's own PIN. No
`user_id` in the request — there is nothing here a caller could point
at someone else's account. Never touched by Vendor provisioning
(`ProvisionCompanyRequest` has no PIN field, and never will).

Not gated by `require_subscription_ok`: the whole `/auth/*` surface is
identity/session mechanics exempt from the mutation gate (same as
`logout`/`pin-switch`, enforced by
`test_identity_auth_mechanics_are_never_gated_by_subscription_state`) —
a suspended company's owner must still be able to set a PIN and get
into the app to see why (ADR-009's "all data visible" even suspended),
the same reasoning that already keeps login/logout/pin-switch open.

post.description:
Owner-only (docs/02 §12); bounded by the vendor-set seat limit
(`errors.employees.seat_limit_reached` when there is no room, unless
`seat_limit` is null — unlimited).

patch.description:
Activate/deactivate and/or change role in one call. Reactivating
counts against the seat limit like creation does; the last active Owner
can never be deactivated or demoted (`errors.employees.
last_owner_protected`).

CompanySummary.title: CompanySummary
CompanySummary.description:
Administrative metadata only (ADR-BOS-009 §Vendor data visibility) —
never tenant operational data. `seat_usage` closes a gap flagged in the
Company Provisioning slice: ADR-BOS-009 lists it as vendor-visible
metadata alongside `seat_limit`, deferred only until Tenant Employee
Management (docs/business-os/18 §9 phase 7) gave it something to count.

CustomerCompanyRequisites.title: CustomerCompanyRequisites
CustomerCompanyRequisites.description:
Buyer-company legal requisites for a future Invoice.buyer snapshot
(docs/ACCOUNTANT_REVIEW.md §4 B1, LAW-CONFIRMED core list) — replaces
the previously fully-unconstrained `dict[str, Any]`; `extra="forbid"`
is the allow-list enforcement point, same pattern as the seller-side
`CompanyRequisitesPatch`. No separate VAT-number field, by the same
reasoning §3 R2 applies to the seller: for a domestic company it is
always "BG" + eik, so nothing independent needs storing (international/
reverse-charge buyers are out of scope for V1).

CustomerListItemOut.title: CustomerListItemOut
CustomerListItemOut.description:
GET /customers only — adds the active-order count the list row needs
(docs/15 §6.7) without touching CustomerOut's other callers.

EntitlementResponse.title: EntitlementResponse
EntitlementResponse.description:
Mirrors `service.EntitlementResult` field-for-field. `active_modules`
is the company's full set *after* this call — a vendor UI can render it
directly without a second GET.

OrderDetailOut.title: OrderDetailOut

OrderListItemOut.title: OrderListItemOut
OrderListItemOut.description:
GET /orders only — adds the joined display fields the Kanban/list board
needs (docs/15 §6.3) without touching OrderOut's other callers.

PlatformAdminMe.title: PlatformAdminMe
PlatformAdminMe.description:
Deliberately narrow: who you are and the CSRF token you need. No
`company_id` field exists here because a Vendor Administrator has no
company — this response shape is where that stops being a comment and
becomes a contract.

ProvisionCompanyResponse.title: ProvisionCompanyResponse
ProvisionCompanyResponse.description:
Mirrors `service.ProvisionResult` field-for-field — the HTTP shape of
the provisioning contract, not a place to add response-only fields of
its own.
